title: The Cairene Youth the Barber and the Captain

keywords: the cairene youth the barber and the captain
full_text:
In the vibrant Khan al-Khalili bazaar of Cairo, a high-spirited young student named Karim was getting his head shaved in Master Salim's barbershop. The barber was notorious for talking incessantly and gesticulating wildly with his razor in hand.

As Master Salim leaned out the shop window to shout a comment to a passing donkey driver, his razor accidentally caught the feather plume of a passing Captain of the Janissaries, cleanly slicing the magnificent ostrich feather in two!

The fierce Captain whirled around with eyes blazing, drawing his broad yatagan sword:
'Insolent dog! Thou hast insulted the imperial guard! Prepare to die!'

Master Salim dropped his razor and fainted onto the floor tiles.
Karim, sitting in the barber's chair with his head half-lathered in white soap foam, leaped up, grabbed a towel, bowed with exaggerated courtly elegance, and cried:

'Hold, noble Captain of the Citadel! Do not sheath thy blade in ordinary flesh! My barber is a certified imperial stylist trained in the palaces of Constantinople! He saw that thy magnificent plume was four inches too long according to the latest decree of the Grand Vizier! He performed the delicate imperial cut to ensure thy helmet meets the highest standard of palace fashion!'

The Captain paused, bewildered, looking from his sliced feather to Karim's completely solemn face and lathered scalp.
'Palace fashion?' muttered the Captain.
'Indeed!' affirmed Karim. 'Look how aerodynamic and martial thy helmet appears now! Even the Sultan's chief falconer wears his plume at that exact angle!'

The Captain looked into the barber's bronze mirror, admired his new silhouette, and sheathed his sword with a broad grin:
'By Allah, youth, thou art right! It looks far more ferocious!'
He tossed a silver coin to the trembling barber, patted Karim on the shoulder, and marched proudly down the street.

When he was gone, Master Salim sat up, gasping:
'Karim, my son, thy quick tongue saved my throat!'
Karim washed the soap from his brow and laughed:
'A handful of wit and a courteous tongue are better than a thousand shields when dealing with angry soldiers!'
moral: Presence of mind and good humor defuse volatile misunderstandings into moments of shared laughter.
